rfm_tuples.R: The Company was in compliance with its debt covenants as of December 31, 2024. (10-K, Note 7, Indebtedness)
rfm_tuples.f: claim_evolution + 10-Q follow-up — verify whether the 'in compliance' assertion was re-affirmed in the next 10-Q (Q1 2025) without amendment, or whether covenant trips emerged at the property/Fund level after the cutoff date of the assertion.
rfm_tuples.M_value: Q1 2025 10-Q discloses NEW INFORMATION: 'a Fund V mortgage of $35.4 million, or $7.1 million at the Company's share, had not met its debt service coverage ratio requirement.' The 10-K covenant compliance assertion is technically true as of 12/31/24 — but a Fund V property-level mortgage tripped its DSC test by 3/31/25 (within ~90 days of 10-K filing). Filing notes 'this is not an event of default, the debt maturity was not accelerated' — i.e., DSC trip triggers a cash trap / sweep, not acceleration. Disclosed plainly in the 10-Q.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Mode B catch — the 10-K's 'in compliance' headline is technically accurate, but a Fund V property-level DSC covenant tripped within one quarter. The amount is small ($7.1M Acadia share of $35.4M total) and disclosure in the 10-Q is forthright, but the speed of the transition from blanket 'in compliance' to a named covenant trip suggests the underlying property cash flows were already deteriorating at the 10-K date. Mild forensic flag, not fraud.

rfm_tuples.R: Auditor history: Deloitte & Touche LLP — 'We have served as the Company's auditor since 2023.' Predecessor: BDO USA, LLP — 'We served as the Company's auditor from 2005 to 2022.'
rfm_tuples.f: auditor_change_tracker — 17-year BDO tenure ended at YE2022; Deloitte engaged for 2023+. Verify whether the change was a Big-4 upgrade (positive) or accompanied by reportable events (disagreements / material weakness).

The change is a Big-4 UPGRADE (BDO USA -> Deloitte) — generally a positive forensic signal. Deloitte issued unqualified opinion 2024-02-14 on FY2024; critical audit matter is impairment of real estate investments (routine for REITs). BDO's prior opinion (FY2022) was also unqualified. Two-year Deloitte tenure now.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Auditor history is clean. Long-tenured BDO replaced by Deloitte in 2023 — a Big-4 upgrade, not a downgrade or distress-driven change. No disagreements or material weaknesses. The critical audit matter (real-estate impairment) is the expected REIT focus area.

rfm_tuples.R: During the years ended December 31, 2024, 2023 and 2022, no single tenant or property collectively comprised more than 10% of the Company's Total revenues.
rfm_tuples.f: revenue_concentration / self_text — verify there is no hidden tenant concentration risk. Cross-check the Top Tenants table for largest tenant by ABR % and any single-property dependence.

rfm_tuples.R: Scheduled debt principal repayments: 2025 = $477.6M (31% of total $1.548B). The Company has extended the Revolver to April 15, 2028 and the $400M Term Loan to April 15, 2028 (Sept 2024 amendment). Revolver capacity raised to $525M with $1.1B accordion.
rfm_tuples.f: Mode B — derive whether the 31% near-term maturity wall is a refinancing risk or already addressed via the credit-facility extension + ATM equity raises. Cross-check the 2025 maturity composition (property mortgages vs corporate debt).
rfm_tuples.M_source: self_text (10-K Note 7 + 10-K LCR section + 8-K 2025-02-14 ATM agreement)
rfm_tuples.M_value: Bulk of the $477.6M 2025 maturity wall is property-level mortgages (each ~$30-90M). Corporate unsecured (Revolver $525M, Term Loan $400M, Senior Notes $100M issued Aug 2024 maturing 2027/2029) is staggered post-2025. Company raised $732M net via equity (33.8M shares) in 2024, ended FY24 with new $500M ATM (entered Feb 14 2025 same day as 10-K) of which $443.7M still available at 3/31/25, and just extended the unsecured credit facility to 2028. Multiple property mortgages were extended in 2024. Q1 2025 10-Q shows the Company actively acquiring ($326M Core + $68M IM = $394.5M acquisitions in Q1 alone), not playing defense.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: The 2025 maturity wall looks scary in isolation but is fully addressed by (i) the September 2024 unsecured credit-facility extension to 2028, (ii) $732M of 2024 equity raised, (iii) the new $500M ATM with $443.7M dry-powder at 3/31/25, and (iv) active asset recycling. Management is offensive (Q1 acquisitions $394.5M), not defensive — consistent with a REIT that has refinancing capacity.

rfm_tuples.R: Issuance of Common Shares — 'During the year ended December 31, 2024, we raised net proceeds of $732.0 million through the issuance of 33.8 million shares from primary offerings and our ATM program.' Plus Feb 2025 entered new $500M ATM (replacing terminated $400M ATM).
rfm_tuples.f: Mode B — derive whether the heavy equity issuance is offensive (funding accretive acquisitions) or defensive (plugging operating cash burn / refinancing). Compare share count growth vs dividend per share trajectory.
rfm_tuples.M_value: Share count: ~99M (early 2024) -> 121.3M weighted avg Q1 2025 -> 130.96M (April 25 2025). Dilution ~32% in ~15 months. HOWEVER: dividend per share was RAISED from $0.18 to $0.20 quarterly ($0.72 -> $0.80 annualized) for Q1 2025 — and per-share dividend would not be raised through ~30% dilution unless management saw FFO/share holding up. Q1 2025 acquisitions ($394.5M) and 2024 acquisitions are the use of proceeds. Forward sales (10.9M ATM forward shares outstanding) match-fund deals. Equity issuance is OFFENSIVE.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Mode B catch in the opposite direction — heavy dilution combined with a dividend RAISE and aggressive acquisition pace is a positive signal: management is monetizing public-equity capital at premium-to-NAV pricing to fund accretive growth. This is the inverse of a defensive ATM. Forensic 'cash burn / refinancing' read is rejected.

rfm_tuples.R: Implied claim — for a REIT with $1.55B of consolidated debt, insider behavior should not show cluster-selling around the heavy equity issuance windows or covenant trip dates.
rfm_tuples.f: insider_vs_calendar / form4 — parse all Form 4 transactions Jan 2024 through May 15 2025 (44 filings). Classify as grants/RSU-vests vs open-market sales. Check CEO/CFO behavior around the Jan 2024 follow-on offering, Oct 2024 follow-on offering, and the Feb 2025 $500M ATM launch.
rfm_tuples.M_value: Of 44 Form 4 filings: 0 open-market sales (no Code S without paired Code C from option exercise). 1 open-market BUY: Director Zoba purchased 1,000 sh on 2024-03-19 (Code P, $1k position add). Routine RSU/LTIP grants to officers (Code A): CEO Bernstein +189,316 sh (Feb 2025) + 125,197 sh (Feb 2025 PSU vest) + 242,148 sh (Feb 2024) + 59,760 sh (Jan 2024) — all grants/vests, no sales. Tax-withholding sales (Code F via Code C exercise): CFO Gottfried 12,500 sh (May 2024) and 12,000 sh (Feb 2025); other officers similar small amounts. Total non-grant share dispositions across all officers ~175K shares vs 1.23M shares of grants/acquisitions. Insiders are net BUYERS via comp, with no open-market selling.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Insider behavior is clean. No clustered selling around the Jan 2024 / Oct 2024 / Feb 2025 capital-markets events. Director Zoba's $19k open-market buy is a directional positive (small but only such trade). CEO and CFO showed no open-market sales in the 16-month pre-cutoff window.

rfm_tuples.R: Total Core Portfolio: 5.12M sq ft, 93.1% leased / 95.8% occupied. ABR $164.6M, $36.51/sq ft (10-K, Item 2 Properties table).
rfm_tuples.f: Verify Core occupancy is stable into Q1 2025; check whether any geographic market is materially weaker.
rfm_tuples.M_value: Q1 2025 Core Portfolio operating GLA: 5.09M sq ft (vs 5.12M at YE24), occupancy 91.6% (Acadia share 91.7%). Headline metric DROPPED ~3-4pp from YE24's 95.8% occupancy. Geographic mix Q1 25: Chicago Metro 83.9%, NY Metro 93.0%, LA Metro 100%, SF Metro 0.0% (2 dev assets, no operating GLA), Dallas Metro 88.6%, DC Metro 79.8%, Boston Metro 100%, Suburban 93.9%. Weakness in Chicago (83.9%) and DC Metro (79.8%) — driven by 840 N. Michigan Avenue (Chicago, 91.9% Acadia interest) which is the same asset that went through 2023+2024 debt-extinguishment restructuring. SF Metro showing 0% operating GLA = redevelopment, not vacancy.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: The 95.8% YE24 occupancy headline does not survive into Q1 25 (91.6%) — but the gap is largely the inclusion of properties moved into operating GLA from development pipeline and the persistence of weakness at 840 N. Michigan (chronic distressed asset that has been restructured twice). Disclosure is straightforward but the headline 95.8% number flatters relative to the operating reality.

rfm_tuples.R: Impairment charges on properties totaled $1.7M in 2024 vs $3.7M in 2023. '840 N. Michigan Avenue' had a debt-extinguishment restructuring in BOTH 2024 and 2023, plus an impairment in 2022.
rfm_tuples.f: Mode B — derive whether the modest 2024 impairment understates the underlying property-level distress at the Chicago Magnificent Mile asset. Check the structured-financing portfolio for credit migration.
rfm_tuples.M_value: 840 N. Michigan was impaired in 2022, restructured (gain on debt extinguishment) 2023 and 2024 — a chronic-distress trophy asset on Chicago Magnificent Mile. The structured-financing portfolio has CECL allowance up from $1.28M (YE23) to $2.00M (YE24) to $2.13M (Q1 25) with $725K provision in 2024 vs $381K in 2023 (+90% YoY). Q1 2025 subsequent event: a $54.0M preferred-equity-recharacterized-as-note-receivable was MODIFIED to extend maturity from Feb 25, 2025 to Feb 9, 2027 with $25.3M accrued interest catch-up paid by the borrower — i.e., a workout that was disclosed as 'subsequent event' AFTER the borrower had been carrying $25.3M of unpaid PIK-type accrual.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Mode B catch — the $1.7M FY24 impairment headline understates the property-level distress. Two consecutive years of debt-extinguishment restructurings at 840 N. Michigan, +90% YoY growth in structured-financing credit-loss provision, and the Q1 2025 modification of a $54M note where $25.3M of interest had accrued unpaid all suggest the structured-financing portfolio carries embedded credit risk that is being managed through extension/modification rather than mark-down. Honest but selective framing in MD&A.

rfm_tuples.M_value: Net income ATTRIBUTABLE TO ACADIA SHAREHOLDERS was actually POSITIVE $1.6M in Q1 25 vs $3.3M in Q1 24 — basic/diluted EPS $0.01 (vs $0.03 prior). summary: AKR is a moderately-honest open-air retail REIT 10-K with disclosure that is consistent into the Q1 2025 10-Q but contains three Mode B selective-framing items. (1) The 10-K's 'in compliance with debt covenants' assertion is technically true at 12/31/24 but a Fund V property-level DSC covenant tripped by 3/31/25 ($7.1M Acadia share, no acceleration). (2) Headline Core Portfolio occupancy dropped from 95.8% (YE24) to 91.6% (Q1 25) — mostly due to 840 N. Michigan chronic distress (restructured twice in 2023+2024) and inclusion of redevelopment assets. (3) Structured-financing portfolio carries embedded credit risk — $54M note had $25.3M of accrued unpaid interest that was paid at the Q1 25 modification, and CECL allowance grew +90% YoY. Counterbalancing strong positives: Big-4 auditor upgrade (BDO->Deloitte, 2023+), no going-concern language, zero insider open-market sales across 44 Form 4 filings in 16 months pre-cutoff, dividend RAISED 11% (from $0.18 to $0.20 quarterly) for Q1 25, $443.7M of ATM dry powder, credit facility extended to 2028, clean counterparty mirror, no tenant >10% of revenue, aggressive Q1 25 acquisition pace ($394.5M). The -21.6% pre-cutoff drawdown looks sector-correlated (retail REIT / rate-sensitive) plus dilution-driven (32% share-count growth in 15 months) rather than honest-disclosure failure. Framework would tag this as cleaner-than-headline-drawdown suggests but with chronic Magnificent Mile distress as a real overhang.
